page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-224 is a compute-focused virtual machine instance built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 224 dedicated vCPUs derived from 112 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor, executing two threads per core. Memory provisioned to the instance totals 224.0 GB, establishing a lean ratio of 1.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware cache provisions include 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. The platform includes AES, VAES, and SHA-NI cryptographic instruction support, alongside AVX vector acceleration, though it lacks AVX-512 extensions and AMX units. No local disk storage is bundled with this instance, and it does not contain GPU hardware.

Benchmark data reveals high multi-threaded compute and throughput capabilities. Multi-core performance in stress-ng ranks in the top ten percent at 302,087.45, paired with a top-tier PassMark CPU score of 113,943.63 and strong encryption test throughput at 231,240.59. Physics simulations and ray tracing also achieve top-decile ratings. In-memory operations demonstrate notable efficiency, logging 186.57 million Redis SET operations per second and cached memory bandwidth of 13,016.92 GB/sec. Large block uncached memory transfers register at 285.12 GB/sec for reads and 131.75 GB/sec for writes. Single-core evaluations, including Geekbench single-core at 1,608.0 and gzip compression at 27.51 GB/sec, place in the middle tier.

The 1:1 memory-to-vCPU allocation provides economical resource density for workloads that prioritize raw compute over large resident memory sets. Users do not pay for surplus memory capacity that parallel execution threads would leave unutilized. Conversely, this constraint presents tradeoffs; workloads requiring massive datasets in memory or intensive large-model LLM generation will be bounded by memory headroom and lack of GPU acceleration, as illustrated by bottom-quartile throughput on 70B parameter text generation. As a result, the instance is best suited for parallel batch processing, Clang software builds, physics simulations, static web serving, and distributed caching nodes.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-224 is a compute-heavy instance designed for parallel execution tasks requiring dense CPU capacity. Powered by AMD EPYC 7B13 processors, the system delivers 224 dedicated vCPUs across 112 physical cores operating on the x86_64 architecture, alongside 224 GB of total system memory. This 1 GB per vCPU configuration offers high core density without the cost overhead of unneeded memory allocation. The instance does not include integrated local storage or GPU hardware. Performance evaluation shows top-tier multi-core computing metrics, reflected in exceptional stress-ng parallel scores, top-tier PassMark CPU and encryption results, and strong Clang software compilation marks. In-memory operations also achieve high rates, such as 186.57 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks. Given the low RAM-to-CPU ratio, the server is suitable for CPU-bound parallel workloads, software build farms, physics modeling, and high-throughput static web serving rather than large-model inference or memory-heavy databases.
